report_name: Anubis Ransomware Claims Attack on Coca-Cola's Fairlife Dairy

threat_actors.name: Anubis
threat_actors.description: A ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group active since at least December 2024. The group claimed responsibility for the cyberattack on Fairlife, employing double-extortion tactics by encrypting data and threatening to leak 1 TB of exfiltrated information from the company's dark web leak site.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware deployment and data leakage threats.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Anubis ransomware group claimed to have fully encrypted Fairlife's Nutanix infrastructure to disrupt operations.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: As part of its double-extortion tactic, the Anubis group claimed to have exfiltrated 1 terabyte of confidential data from Fairlife's network before deploying the ransomware.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Anubis ransomware likely attempted to prevent recovery by deleting volume shadow copies using the vssadmin.exe utility, a common tactic for this type of malware.

malware.name: Anubis Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the Anubis group to encrypt Fairlife's systems, specifically targeting its Nutanix infrastructure. The malware reportedly includes a 'wiper mode' capability, allowing for the permanent destruction of data.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: The vssadmin.exe utility was likely used by the attackers to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery from backups.

tools.name: PsExec
tools.description: The PsExec utility was likely used by the Anubis group for lateral movement and remote execution within Fairlife's network.

tools.name: WMIC
tools.description: The WMIC utility was likely abused by the Anubis group for lateral movement and remote execution.

identities.name: Fairlife
identities.description: A U.S.-based dairy producer and subsidiary of The Coca-Cola Company, targeted by the Anubis ransomware group. The attack disrupted production and involved the encryption of its Nutanix infrastructure and exfiltration of 1 TB of data.

identities.name: The Coca-Cola Company
identities.description: The parent company of Fairlife. The company disclosed the cyberattack on its subsidiary on July 16, 2026.

infrastructure.name: Anubis Dark Web Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A site on the dark web used by the Anubis ransomware group to list its victims and threaten the publication of stolen data. Fairlife was listed on this site on July 20, 2026.

infrastructure.name: Anubis Data Exfiltration Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Servers controlled by the Anubis group used to store the 1 TB of confidential data allegedly stolen from Fairlife.

indicators.name: Anubis Ransomware VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: Anubis Ransomware VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 9b1d8f3a-4c6e-4b8d-9f0a-1b2c3d4e5f6a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware like Anubis to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/ransomware-group-threatening-to-leak-data-stolen-from-coca-colas-fairlife/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-23
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a technique associated with Anubis ransomware to prevent system recovery.

indicators.name: Anubis Lateral Movement using PsExec or WMIC
indicators.pattern:
title: Anubis Lateral Movement using PsExec or WMIC
id: 8c0a7b29-5d5f-4a7c-8e9b-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of PsExec or WMIC for remote process creation, a common lateral movement technique used by ransomware groups like Anubis.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/ransomware-group-threatening-to-leak-data-stolen-from-coca-colas-fairlife/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-23
tags:
  - attack.t1021.002
  - attack.t1047
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_psexec:
    OriginalFileName: 'psexec.c'
    Image|endswith: '.exe'
  selection_wmic:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'process call create'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity.
indicators.description: Detects the use of PsExec or WMIC for remote execution, a lateral movement technique likely used by the Anubis group.
